passage:
"Vaibhav, time to go home now."
"No! Swing!"
"One more push, then home."
Yamini gave one push. "Okay, all done."
"No! No! Swing!"
Vaibhav's face crumpled. His hands gripped the chains. His legs went stiff.
"Come, baby. Mumma's here."
"Nooo!"
He started to cry, big tears rolling down.

qa.q: What did Vaibhav say when told it was time to go home?
qa.a: Vaibhav said, "No! Swing!"

qa.q: What was Vaibhav feeling when his face crumpled?
qa.a: He felt sad and angry about leaving, and he could not handle the wish to stay.

qa.q: What could Yamini do at this first moment?
qa.a: She could name his feeling, like "You love the swing," and give a simple warning before leaving, staying calm as he cries.

qa.q: How might Yamini be feeling as Vaibhav starts crying?
qa.a: She may feel tired or worried about the scene, but she can see he is only little and upset.

grounding: It shows a toddler told it is time to leave the park who cannot manage the wish to stay, so his face crumples, his body stiffens and he cries.

passage:
Babysitter's note, Thursday.
At the park at five, I told Uday it was time to go. He was in the sandpit. He looked up, and his lip started to shake. He held his spade tight. When I held out my hand, he went stiff all over and threw his head back. Then he cried loudly. I knelt and said, "You wanted to stay. It's hard to go."
— Harsha

qa.q: Where was Uday when it was time to go?
qa.a: Uday was in the sandpit.

qa.q: What did Uday's shaking lip show?
qa.a: It showed he was getting upset and frustrated at having to leave.

qa.q: What did Harsha do that helped?
qa.a: Harsha knelt and named Uday's feeling, which helps a toddler feel understood.

qa.q: How might Uday's parents feel reading the note?
qa.a: They may feel reassured that Harsha stayed kind and calm when Uday got upset.

grounding: It illustrates a toddler told to leave the park who cannot manage wanting to stay, so his lip shakes, his body stiffens and he cries.

passage:
Daycare note, Tuesday

Darshan (2) had a hard pick-up today. His father arrived while Darshan was playing in the sand pit. When his father said, "Time to go home," Darshan looked up and his face crumpled. He held a spade tightly and his whole body went rigid. Then he began to cry loudly.

I think he wasn't ready to leave his game. I sat close and said, "You want to stay." His father waited with him.

— Sarita, room carer

qa.q: Where was Darshan playing when his father arrived?
qa.a: In the sand pit.

qa.q: Why did Darshan's face crumple?
qa.a: He felt sad and frustrated, not ready to leave his game, and couldn't manage the wish to stay.

qa.q: What did the adults do that helped?
qa.a: Sarita sat close and named his wish to stay, and his father waited with him instead of rushing.

qa.q: How might Darshan's father feel at this pick-up?
qa.a: He may feel a little tired and unsure, but patient enough to wait.

grounding: A daycare carer's note shows two-year-old Darshan's face crumpling, body stiffening and crying when told it is time to leave his game.

passage:
At the village fair near Jorhat, Bhupen had been riding the little wooden horse for a long time. The man running the ride tapped his watch.

"Bhupen, come. Time to go," said Pankaj, his father, reaching out.

Bhupen held the horse's ears tightly. His face crumpled. His legs went stiff and straight.

"No! Horse!"

"We have to go now."

Bhupen's mouth opened wide, and the crying began, loud enough that people turned to look. Pankaj bent down beside him, close.

qa.q: What was Bhupen riding at the fair?
qa.a: The little wooden horse.

qa.q: What do Bhupen's crumpled face and stiff legs show?
qa.a: They show he feels sad and frustrated, unable to manage his wish to keep riding.

qa.q: What could Pankaj do next?
qa.a: Stay close and calm, name Bhupen's wish to stay, and lift him off gently without lecturing.

qa.q: How might Pankaj feel when people turn to look?
qa.a: He may feel a little embarrassed, but he stays close to Bhupen.

grounding: At a village fair, toddler Bhupen is told it is time to leave the ride; his face crumples, his body stiffens and he starts to cry.

passage: In a London park, two-year-old Tariq was pouring sand into a bucket beside his friend Yuki. "Time to go home now," Mama said, holding out her hand. Tariq looked at the bucket, then at Yuki, still digging. His face crumpled. His arms went stiff at his sides. "No!" he wailed, and big tears rolled down as Mama bent to pick him up.

qa.q: What was Tariq doing beside Yuki?
qa.a: He was pouring sand into a bucket.

qa.q: Why did Tariq's face crumple when Mama said it was time to go?
qa.a: He felt upset and frustrated, wanting to stay and play with Yuki but not yet able to manage that wish.

qa.q: What could Mama try next time before leaving the park?
qa.a: She could give a small warning, like 'two more buckets, then home', and name his feeling: 'You want to stay with Yuki.'

qa.q: What might Yuki experience when Tariq is carried away crying?
qa.a: Yuki may feel puzzled or a little sad to lose a digging friend so suddenly.

grounding: Shows a toddler told it is time to leave the park, unable to manage the wish to stay, crumpling into tears with a stiff body.
